Subject: Svc account rollout + auth ops plan / FinLytics — post-demo follow-up

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the FinLytics team. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the integration path and auth approach.

Recap (integration areas we covered)
- SDKs: JS for the web UI (low-latency calls), Python for batch reranker/embeddings pipelines.
- Auth options: short-lived API keys vs service-account JWTs (recommended for server-to-server).
- Routing: region-aware routing (us-east primary, eu fallback) and model-tiering for cost control.
- Structured output/tool-calling: plan to use function-calling for your data enrichment step.
- Embeddings & rerankers: dense vectors stored in your vector DB; we'll provide embedding model suggestions and a lightweight reranker template.

Recommended auth ops plan (high level)
1) Short term (POC): Issued scoped API keys with 30 day rotation policy (manual via Console).
2) Production: Service account + JWT flow issued from your identity provider -> Redwood trusts JWTs (RS256) or you can use our signed short-lived credentials.
3) Key rotation & audits: Integrate KMS (GCP/Azure/AWS) to store private keys; Redwood will rotate verification keys on our side.
4) Least privilege: create separate service accounts per environment (prod/staging) and per major workload (ingest/online-serving).

Attachments: architecture notes and rollout checklist attached. I put a short implementation checklist in the spreadsheet that maps to the tasks below.

Proposed next steps
- Can we schedule a 90-minute architecture workshop next Tuesday to walk through the service-account flow and routing policies? (Rishi, Marissa, engineering + FinLytics infra)
- For the workshop, please share any existing key management constraints (KMS tenant, HSM requirements, compliance needs).
- Tom/Sam: confirm if you prefer JWT (IdP-issued) or Redwood-managed service credentials for Prod.

If that plan looks good I'll loop in our infra engineer (Ben) and send a calendar invite with the pre-read.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks for confirming the IdP/JWT direction, Sam. Notes inline and a few concrete asks below:

Inline answers
- Okta/JWT: Redwood supports RS256 verification of IdP-signed JWTs. We'll provide a verification key endpoint you can pin in your Okta app config. We can also accept SAML-backed service tokens if needed.
- POC API keys: we'll generate scoped keys with a single role (ingest:write, serve:read) and a 30-day expiry flag; keys are revocable from the Console.
- HSM: if FinLytics requires HSM for private key storage we can accept JWT public keys and keep verification on our side — your KMS/HSM stays in front of signing.
- Embedding throughput: for the embedding model we recommended (redwood-mini-embed), estimate ~0.7ms/token on our infra; for 250k rows (avg 100 tokens) expect approximately X compute hours — I'll have Ben produce a cost/throughput calc before the workshop.

Concrete asks before the architecture workshop
1) Share Okta metadata endpoint and allowed audience claim you expect for tokens (so we can validate token acceptance).
2) Confirm if procurement needs a separate statement of work for key rotations/HSM integrations.
3) Any specific retention or audit window requirements for token logs (our default is 90 days, can extend).

I'll draft a short tech pre-read (5–6 slides) and include a proposed workshop agenda. Ben will add the cost model for embeddings/serving.

I'll send the invite for Tuesday 9:30 PT unless someone objects.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
